findings.title: J500 bench-PSU input has no over-voltage element; the replica over-charge trip does not block current into the FC, which has 10 V MLCCs on Dir_Chrg_In/VBATT_SENSE/VBUSP and BQ25886 SYS (12 V abs max)
findings.location: battery_protection_replica: J500.1 (202.92,165.2) = Dir_Chrg_In -> R109 -> VBATT_SENSE (C42) -> inhibits -> VBUSP (C1, C3); JP510 -> CHG_SYS (U511.15/16). J500 silk B+/MID/B- at y=162.6; nearest VSOLAR terminal J400 '+' at (229.76,161.7)
findings.description: The only limit on J500 voltage is the sheet text 'BENCH PSU WINDOW 4.9 V <= V <= 8.4 V'. The R5460 replica does not guard against a supply set too high. Above VDET1 (8.5 V) it opens COUT, so Q501 turns off. That blocks charge-direction current only: discharge current runs FC GND -> B- -> Q501 source-to-drain, which is Q501's body-diode forward direction. The full PSU voltage therefore still reaches Dir_Chrg_In. That node feeds VBATT_SENSE C42 and, with the inhibit shunts fitted, VBUSP C1/C3. All three are LCSC C19702 (10 uF 10 V X5R 0603). With JP510 fitted it also reaches BQ25886 SYS (abs max 12 V, converter off). The same bench uses 12-18 V on the 5.08 mm screw terminals J400/J401, about 17 mm away. Item 7 added an '18V MAX' legend and a pre-session OVP check for those terminals, but J500 got neither. Someone who reuses the VSOLAR supply or leaves it at 12-18 V would put 1.2-1.8x rated voltage on FC-copy caps, through a 2 A limit. That is the outcome item 7 was written to prevent. This is new exposure: the flight pack cannot exceed 8.4 V, so heritage never saw it.
findings.evidence: netlist: J500.1 = Dir_Chrg_In; C42.1 = VBATT_SENSE, C1.1/C3.1 = VBUSP; project.db C1/C3/C42/C40 = C19702 (10 V X5R per final_list item 7). Q501 pins 1-3 = B- (source), 5-8 = PROT_DRAIN. R5460 EA: VDET1 4.250 V/cell -> COUT. BQ25886 SLUSD88A 7.1: BAT, SYS -0.3..12 V. PCB silk: '18V MAX' at (233,171.2)/(245.5,171.2); no voltage legend near J500 (B+/MID/B- only)
findings.recommendation: This rev, text and silk only: add 'PSU OVP <= 9 V, verify trip with J500 disconnected before each session' to the sheet note and bench procedure, mirroring item 7. If a silk edit is still open, put an '8.4V MAX' legend at J500. Next rev: an OV cut-off on J500.1 (Zener-gated PMOS or OVP load switch opening at ~9 V), or a crowbar Zener plus PTC on Dir_Chrg_In ahead of the J14 stub.
findings.reference: BQ25886 SLUSD88A 7.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings; Nisshinbo R5460 EA datasheet (over-charge detection turns off COUT only); FlatSat review 2026-10-21 item 7 (same 10 V C19702 rationale for VSOLAR)

findings.title: In Mode 2 (USB charger) the ISS inhibit and the protection replica are bypassed: the charger returns through board GND, not B-
findings.location: battery_protection_replica: U511 PGND/EP = GND, J510 GND; FC B- = Q501 S = J14.2/4/6/8, reaches GND only through J15/J19/JP607 (JP607 at 217.7,145.79)
findings.description: The sheet says B- 'reaches GND only through the ISS inhibit J15/J19'. That holds in Mode 1, where the floating PSU returns through VBAT_BENCH_N -> Q500/Q501 -> B- -> ISS shunt. Mode 2 is different. Since item 1, U511 SYS drives Dir_Chrg_In, and the charger's return is board GND, so FC load current never passes through B-. Opening the ISS inhibit (removing JP607 and unplugging J15/J19) leaves the FC powered. Only the high-side S1/S2/P1/P2/RBF chain and SW600 still act. The R5460 replica is also out of the path. In Mode 2, any inhibit-matrix or 'ISS inhibit de-powers the bus' check passes the wrong way. A bench user who thinks the ISS inhibit has made the bus safe still has a live FC. The Mode 2 sheet line and the J500 mode-table silk do not say this.
findings.evidence: netlist: B- = C503.2 J14.2/4/6/8 J15.1 J19.1/3 JP607.1 Q501.1-3 R502.2 R505.2 TP502.1; J15.2/J19.2/J19.4/JP607.2 = GND; U511.4/5 = GND; JP510.1 = CHG_SYS, JP510.2 = Dir_Chrg_In. Sheet text: 'Mode 2 USB charger: JP500 OPEN, JP510 fitted ... The FC runs from U511 SYS'
findings.recommendation: This rev: add to the Mode 2 sheet line and the bench procedure: 'ISS inhibit (J15/J19/JP607) and the R5460 replica are not in circuit in Mode 2; run inhibit-matrix and protection tests in Mode 1 only.' Next rev, if Mode 2 should exercise ISS: float the charger return or route it through B-, for example an isolated 5 V input or charger PGND tied to B- behind its own reverse-blocking.
findings.reference: FlatSat sheet battery_protection_replica net-name note (B- through ISS inhibit only); brief hard rule 6 (inhibit chain fidelity)

findings.title: Item 3 ATP probes TP503/TP504 gate drive, which is referenced to floating VBAT_BENCH_N: an earthed scope ground there, with board GND earthed via J701, bypasses the replica FETs and carries load current through the probe lead
findings.location: battery_protection_replica: TP501 VBAT_BENCH_N (194.0,163.5), TP503 DOUT_GATE, TP504 COUT_GATE; J701 GND -> PC earth
findings.description: Item 3's verification asks the bench to check that TP503/TP504 gate drive stays high under a 2 A load, and that DOUT latches on trip. DOUT_GATE and COUT_GATE are referenced to U500 VSS = VBAT_BENCH_N (TP501), which floats in Mode 1. The natural setup puts a mains-earthed scope ground clip on TP501. With J701 on a desktop PC, board GND is also earthed, so the clip shorts VBAT_BENCH_N to GND around Q500/Q501. When DOUT trips, the load current (up to the 2 A PSU limit) moves into the loop: probe ground lead, scope chassis, mains earth, PC, USB cable. The trip test then reads as 'FC stays up', which is invalid, and a thin probe lead and the host USB ground carry amps. The sheet warns about an earthed PSU negative but not about the test-point reference, and the new ATP points a user at those pins.
findings.evidence: netlist: TP501 = VBAT_BENCH_N = U500.6 VSS = Q500.1-3 S; TP503 = DOUT_GATE (Q500.4), TP504 = COUT_GATE (Q501.4); J701 A1/B1/S1 = GND. final_list item 3 verification: 'TP503/TP504 gate drive stays high, no DOUT latch' at 2.0 A
findings.recommendation: Bench procedure: measure TP503/TP504 with a differential probe or a battery-powered/isolated scope, or unplug J701 and every other earthed connection during replica trip tests. State in the ATP that TP501/503/504 are referenced to VBAT_BENCH_N, not GND. No copper change.
findings.reference: General bench practice for floating-reference measurements (ground-loop through earthed oscilloscope); FlatSat sheet note 'The PSU must FLOAT ... (laptop, scope)'

result.scope_checked:
Parsed netlist.xml and erc.json. Checked, pin by pin against the netlist, the Emulator MCU, Bench IO, Solar and Sensor Emulation, Pyro Inhibit, Solar Power Injection and Battery Replica/Charger sheets. Also read the sheet notes and the first-review final_list.md.

Checked and found clean:
- U200 pin map, GPIO assignments (no duplicates, no pin conflicts), IOVDD/DVDD/VREG_AVDD/USB_OTP/QSPI_IOVDD wiring, and the crystal, flash, BOOTSEL and RUN circuits. The core regulator cell parts are identical to the flown U18 cell.
- J701 and J510 CC 5.1k pull-downs, VBUS tie-offs and D+/D- handling. The 22 ohm USB series resistors match the flown FC.
- Q701-Q703 BSS138 pinout (gate/source/drain). Each gate has a 4.7k pull-down, so the FETs are off when the emulator is unpowered and cannot back-drive FC_RESET, USBBOOT or WDT_DISABLE. Their drains sit on the same nodes as the heritage buttons and J4 jumper.
- All eight TCA4311A buffers: pinout against the TI VSSOP-8 pinout, EN and READY pull-ups, pull-ups on both bus sides, and TCA9548A channel mapping (SD0 F0, SD1 F1, SD2 F2, SD3 F3, SD4 BATT, SD5 F4, SD6 F5, SD7 TOP).
- Face-0 I2C addresses: TMP112 0x48 (ADD0 grounded), VEML6031 0x29, DRV2605L 0x5A. No conflicts.
- Hardware I2C mapping of the seven EMU buses: they split 4 on I2C0 and 3 on I2C1, so they need PIO or time-multiplexing. This is firmware, not a hardware defect.
- Fix 1 netlist: JP510 pin 1 is on CHG_SYS. CHG_BAT carries only C515 and TP512.
- Fix 2 netlist: Dir_Chrg_In lands on J14 pins 1/3/5/7/9, with J16.8 still on the net as a sense tap.
- BQ25886 pin map (TS network, ILIM 750 ohm, ICHGSET 5.62k, VSET/CE/OTG/PG strapping) against the sheet notes and the earlier audit's datasheet pin-table check. I could not open the datasheet PDF text, so electrical limits were taken from the sheet notes.
- R5460 replica topology and the gate-drive polarity of Q500/Q501.
- Pyro-inhibit clamp diodes and PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE wiring.
- VSOLAR injection chain.

ERC triage: all 12 errors are FC heritage (U7 pins 6/7, U1.3, U12, U30, U18 VREG_AVDD, and power symbols on the root and RP2350 sheets). None is in a FlatSat bench sheet. The warnings are library or metadata noise plus unspecified-pin pin_to_pin entries on custom symbols. There are no real electrical errors in the bench sheets.

PCB layout and copper were not reviewed here (outside this dimension).

Result: no defect that would make the bench board fail or damage hardware. One minor next-rev note.

Limitation: the RP2350 and BQ25886 datasheet text was not retrievable, because the PDF fetch returned binary and pdftotext is not installed.

findings.title: Always-on +3V3 pull-ups feed six U200 GPIOs when the emulator USB (J701) is absent; item 8 mitigation covers only the faces
findings.location: solar_emulation R362/R363 (EMU_BATT_SDA/SCL), R372/R373 (EMU_TOP_SDA/SCL), R374 (EMU_FC3V3_SENSE); pyro_inhibit R600/R601 (PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE); all to U200 GPIO10-13, GPIO22, GPIO23
findings.description: The OUT-side pull-ups of the BATT and TOP bus buffers (U315/U316), the FC3V3 sense, and the pyro-inhibit state line all return to the FC +3V3 rail, which is powered whenever the FC runs. U200 is powered only from VBUS_EMU via U202, so with J701 unplugged, which is normal for FC-only bench tests, six U200 GPIO pads sit at about 3.3 V through 4.7k with IOVDD at 0 V. This is the same mechanism the first review's item 8 recorded for the F1-F4 ADC pins. Those items are next-rev with a 'plug J701 before enabling any face switch' rule. That rule does not cover these six pins, because they are live from FC power alone, not from face-switch enables. The pins are 5 V-tolerant GPIO, not the non-FT ADC pins, so I could not confirm that a pad parasitic path exists from the RP2350 datasheet. At most about 0.5-0.7 mA per pin is injected, resistor-limited, so damage is unlikely. The residual risk is a partly-powered, undefined emulator state (3V3_EMU floating up, D201 glowing, possible odd boot) when USB is attached late. It is not a failure of the FC or its buses.
findings.evidence: R362/R363/R372/R373/R374 pin1 = +3V3, pin2 = EMU_BATT_SDA/SCL, EMU_TOP_SDA/SCL, EMU_FC3V3_SENSE, going to U200 pins 14/15/16/17/34. R600 4.7k +3V3 to PYRO_INH_COM, R601 4.7k to U200.35. 3V3_EMU is sourced only by U202 (VIN and EN on VBUS_EMU, J701 only).
findings.recommendation: Next rev: pull up the EMU-side bus lines, the FC3V3 sense and the PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE sense to 3V3_EMU. With the emulator off, the buffer then sees a low OUT side, which isolates the bus. Alternatively, raise these resistors to 47k-100k as already suggested for item 8. This rev: extend the bring-up rule to 'attach J701 before applying FC power or enabling any face switch'. No respin warranted.
findings.reference: RP2350 datasheet, GPIO electrical characteristics: pin input voltage versus IOVDD (not text-verified); first review final_list.md item 8

findings.title: BQ25886 gate-drive decoupling not at the pins: item-4 rework doubled the BTST loop to 8.2 mm on B.Cu, and the REGN cap C516 has always been reached through In1 and 2 vias
findings.location: battery_protection_replica / PCB F.Cu+B.Cu+In1: U511 (277.0,152.2) pin 12 BTST, pin 11 REGN; C512 (280.5,149.3) r90; C516 (277.6,156.7) r90
findings.description: BTST: the item-4 fix moved C512 from (280.75,153.08) to (280.5,149.3) so it sits on the SW run. BTST pin 12 is on the south edge of the QFN, so the BTST net now runs from pin 12 through a 0.46/0.20 via, then 6.1 mm on B.Cu at x=279.4 directly under the SYS/SW pins, cutting the B.Cu GND pour beside the EP thermal pads, then a second via and 1.0 mm of F.Cu to C512.2. Before the fix the run was 3.81 mm, 2 vias, In2. REGN: C516 is rotated with its GND pad (277.6,155.925) facing the IC and its REGN pad facing away. Pin 11 therefore reaches C516.1 through F.Cu 1.9 mm, via (279.01,154.979), In1 4.1 mm, via (276.896,158.179) and F.Cu 1.0 mm: about 7 mm and 2 vias, compared with 2.5 mm in a straight line. The first review did not cover this net. Both caps carry the high-side and low-side gate-drive charge pulses, and the TI layout list asks for them next to the pins on the same side. The likely effect is more ringing between BTST and SW and slower high-side switching, at most a small margin loss against the 6 V BTST-SW abs max. A failure has not been shown.
findings.evidence: PCB now: Net-(U511-BTST) total 8.20 mm, vias (278.725,154.33) and (279.5,148.4) 0.46/0.20, B.Cu segment (279.4,153.65)->(279.4,148.5) w0.25 L5.15. Pre-fix board (git d5876e4): C512 at (280.75,153.08), BTST 3.81 mm. Net-(U511-REGN): pin 11 (277.75,154.162) -> via (279.01,154.979) -> In1 2.99+1.09 mm -> via (276.896,158.179) -> C516.1 (277.6,157.475). Same on both boards. Nearest GND via to C516.2 is 2.32 mm away at (275.489,156.887). SLUSD88A pin table: 'Bypass REGN to GND with a 4.7-uF ceramic capacitor', 'Connect a 47nF bootstrap capacitor from SW to BTST'. Abs max BTST to SW -0.3..6 V.
findings.recommendation: This rev: no copper change. Add BTST-SW (differential, ground-spring probe) and REGN ripple to the item-4 scope gate at ILIM 1.48 A / VBUS 5.25 V. Pass condition: BTST-SW below 5.7 V peak and REGN within its spec band with no ringing below its UVLO. Next rev: put C512 right at pin 12 with its SW pad tied to pins 17/18 on F.Cu with no via (e.g. at the SE corner, sharing the SW neck), rotate C516 180 deg so pad 1 faces pin 11 on a short F.Cu run, and give C516.2 its own GND via.
findings.reference: TI SLUSD88A section 11.1 Layout Guidelines item 4 ('Decoupling capacitors should be placed on the same side of and next to the IC and make trace connection as short as possible'); pin table REGN/BTST; 7.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings

findings.title: C215/C218 swap moved the unfiltered VREG_AVDD segment (filter cap to pin 46) onto In2, 1.27 mm from the LX via/In2 run
findings.description: Before the rework (git 3f00bbe), the copper from C215 (CFILT) to pin 46 was a 3.6 mm F.Cu run. The In2 segment near LX sat upstream of C215, on the R200 side, so the RC filter attenuated anything coupled into it. After the C215/C218 swap the order is reversed. Pin 46 runs F.Cu 1.75 mm, then via (277.783,91.68), then In2 about 3.4 mm, then via (279.082,94.58), then F.Cu to C215.1 and on to R200. The whole 6 mm post-filter path now includes the In2 segment and via that start 1.27-1.29 mm from the LX In2 run and LX via, and run under C217/C218. emulator_replace.md reports only the 3.7 -> 5.6 mm distance. It does not say that the LX-adjacent copper is now on the unfiltered side. The RP2350 hardware design guide calls VREG_AVDD 'very sensitive to noise'. The coupling is small (fF-scale), so this degrades margin and does not show a failure. It adds to the open item-5 VREG concern.
findings.recommendation: This rev: fold into the item-5 bring-up gate. During the 0 -> 150 mA core load step at TP202, also probe VREG_AVDD_EMU at C215 and pin 46 with a short ground. If HF content at pin 46 is more than a few mV above C215, rework by fitting a 100 nF 0402 across pin 46/47 or swapping C215/C218 back. Next rev: with the item-5 copy of the flown U18 cell, keep CFILT adjacent to pin 46 on F.Cu with R200 upstream, as flown C68/R94 are.
findings.reference: Raspberry Pi 'Hardware design with RP2350' (minimal design example, VREG_AVDD RC filter); RP2350 datasheet 6.3 core voltage regulator external components; emulator_replace.md 'One regression to note'

findings.title: Mode 2 power returns through board GND, so the ISS inhibit (JP607/J15/J19) and B- chain has no effect on the FC in Mode 2
findings.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: U511 GND pins 4/19/20/25 = GND; JP510 CHG_SYS -> Dir_Chrg_In; B- (Q501 S, J14.2/4/6/8, J15.1, J19.1/3, JP607.1) reaches GND only through JP607/J15/J19
findings.description: After item 1, Mode 2 feeds the FC battery node from U511 SYS. The charger is referenced to board GND, so the FC load current returns to U511 directly on GND and never goes through B-. In flight, and in bench Mode 1 (J500.3 -> Q500/Q501 -> B- -> JP607/J15/J19 -> GND), the ISS inhibit breaks the pack negative. In Mode 2, opening JP607 or the J15/J19 switches leaves the FC powered. The sheet note says B- 'reaches GND only through the ISS inhibit J15/J19', but the Mode 2 description does not say that the inhibit is bypassed. This creates no damage path. The risk is a false pass or a false failure if an ISS-inhibit or deployment-switch test is run in Mode 2.

Next rev, if Mode 2 must keep inhibit fidelity: return the charger through B- (an isolated or floating 5 V input), which is probably not worth the cost.

findings.title: Via-in-pad rework (batch b1) left C216 (pin-23 DVDD 4.7 uF) and Y200.4 on an F.Cu GND island with no via; return runs through a 0.25 mm link between the crystal pads
findings.description: Batch b1 removed the in-pad GND via on Y200.4 (it was at (274.994,101.570) on base_orig) and replaced it with a 0.25 mm F.Cu link from Y200.4 to Y200.2, running diagonally between the XIN pad (Y200.1) and the XOUT-side pad (Y200.3). On the final board C216.2 and Y200.4 share an F.Cu GND fill island (bbox 274.17-276.06 x 99.58-103.37) that holds no via. The only connection to the GND system is that link, then Y200.2 into the main pour and the via at (271.85,104.375). The return path of the DVDD pin-23 4.7 uF capacitor grows from about 1.6 mm (pad -> trace -> in-pad via) to about 5.1 mm of 0.25 mm trace. That adds roughly 1 nH of loop inductance, about double to triple the capacitor's own mounted ESL. Core transient return current also now flows across the crystal case pads, inside the oscillator's guard. emulator_replace.md notes the longer path ('about 4 mm instead of 1.6 mm') but not that the island has no via. RP2350 DS 6.3.8.1 recommends this second 4.7 uF at DVDD pin 23 for best regulator performance, so its effectiveness drops. This will not stop the emulator working. It does weaken the core-supply decoupling that the item-5 bench gate tests.

verdicts.evidence_checked: Netlist (review2/netlist.xml): R362/R363/R372/R373/R374 pin1 = +3V3, pin2 = EMU_BATT_SDA/SCL, EMU_TOP_SDA/SCL, EMU_FC3V3_SENSE to U200.14/15/16/17/34. RP2350 datasheet (scratchpad/verify/rp2350ds.txt): Table 1674 lists GPIO10, 11, 12, 13, 22 and 23 as 'Digital IO (FT)'. Table 1673 (14.8.2.1) says FT means 'very little current flows into the pin whilst it is below 3.63 V and IOVDD is 0 V'. Table 1680 (14.9.1, abs max) gives VPIN_FT at IOVDD=0V as -0.5..3.63 V. Feature list p.1: 'GPIOs are 5 V-tolerant (powered) and 3.3 V-failsafe (unpowered)'. emulator_mcu.kicad_sch has the note 'PHANTOM POWER PATH (accepted - obey the BENCH RULE)', which covers all 14 device-side 4.7k pull-ups and ends 'BENCH RULE: plug the emulator USB in before or with FC power; never leave the FC powered with the emulator unplugged.' pyro_inhibit.kicad_sch has the note 'WHY R600 PULLS UP TO THE FC +3V3 AND NOT TO 3V3_EMU (review fix, chair-accepted deviation)'. final_list.md item 8 says 'F5 (GPIO24) and FC3V3 (GPIO22) senses are on FT pins.'
verdicts.reasoning: The netlist matches the finding, but the claimed impact and the coverage gap do not hold. (1) The six pins are FT. The RP2350 datasheet makes them 3.3 V failsafe with IOVDD = 0 V: very little current flows, and 3.3 V is inside the 3.63 V abs max. This is the opposite of item 8, which concerned the non-FT GPIO26-29 ADC pins. The first review already set GPIO22 aside as FT for this reason. The ~0.5-0.7 mA injection and the partly-powered emulator state are therefore unsupported for these pins. The reviewer admitted they could not confirm a parasitic path. (2) The claim that the bring-up rule covers only the faces is false. The emulator sheet already documents this exact phantom path for all 14 buffer-side pull-ups as an accepted design choice. Its BENCH RULE says to plug J701 in before or with FC power, which is the same rule the finding proposes. (3) The recommendation to pull R600 up to 3V3_EMU would reverse a documented, chair-accepted fix. With 3V3_EMU unpowered, R600 becomes a pull-down that holds an FC-commanded Deploy EN at ~1.8 V, below the TPS4H160 VIH of 2.0 V, so FC-only deploy runs could silently fail. R601 = 4.7k was chosen deliberately to limit back-feed. No defect remains. At most, the sheet's conservative ESD-diode wording is pessimistic for FT pins.
verdicts.corrected_description: No defect. The six +3V3-pulled U200 pins (GPIO10-13, 22, 23) are FT pads. The RP2350 datasheet makes them 3.3 V failsafe with IOVDD at 0 V (Table 1673/1680). The emulator sheet already documents the FC-powered/emulator-unpowered phantom path as accepted and requires J701 before or with FC power. R600 to +3V3 is a deliberate, documented fix, and moving it to 3V3_EMU would break FC-only deploy tests.

verdicts.evidence_checked: Netlist: U511 pins 4/5/19/20/25 = GND. JP510.1 = /Battery Replica and Bench Power/CHG_SYS and JP510.2 = Dir_Chrg_In. Net B- = C503.2, J14.2/4/6/8, J15.1, J19.1/3, JP607.1, Q501.1-3, R502.2, R505.2 and TP502.1, with no GND member. JP607.2, J15.2 and J19.2/4 = GND. battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch notes: line 13102 'B- = pack negative ... reaches GND only through the ISS inhibit J15/J19'. Line 13201 'Mode 2 USB charger: JP500 OPEN, JP510 fitted, bench PSU disconnected at J500. The FC runs from U511 SYS'. No note says Mode 2 bypasses the B- inhibit. pyro_inhibit.kicad_sch POWER-UP RECIPE: 'bridge JP607 (B- return) + JP606 (RBF) + ONE inhibit path'. This implies B- is needed in every mode. review_fixes.md item 1 moved JP510.1 from CHG_BAT to CHG_SYS. final_list.md line 133 records 'Mode 2 returns through board GND' but not the inhibit consequence.
verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the evidence. In Mode 2, U511 is GND-referenced and drives Dir_Chrg_In through JP510. The FC load current returns to U511 on board GND and never passes through B-, so opening J15, J19 or JP607 does not remove FC power. The positive-side RBF/inhibit chain (JP602-606, J7/J8/J10/J20/J29/J30) still works, because nothing is in series with Dir_Chrg_In. Only the B-side ISS inhibit is bypassed. One correction: the bypass is not caused by item 1. It has existed since D3, because the old CHG_BAT feed was also GND-referenced. It mirrors how any GND-referenced external source on Dir_Chrg_In behaves on the heritage FC. There is no damage path. The impact is limited to test fidelity: an ISS-inhibit or deployment-switch test run in Mode 2 gives a false result. The pyro sheet's power-up recipe also wrongly implies that JP607 is required. This is a text-only fix, so severity is info and the disposition is next-rev or doc this rev.
verdicts.corrected_description: In Mode 2, U511 (GND-referenced, SYS -> JP510 -> Dir_Chrg_In) powers the FC with its return on board GND, so the B-side ISS inhibit (J15/J19, bench shunt JP607) has no effect on FC power. The positive-side RBF/inhibit chain still works. This has been inherent to the D3 charger since before item 1 and was not introduced by the SYS move. The Mode 2 sheet note and the pyro sheet's POWER-UP RECIPE should say that ISS-inhibit/deployment-switch tests must run in Mode 1, and that JP607 is not needed in Mode 2. No hardware change.

verdicts.evidence_checked: netlist.xml: VBAT_BENCH_N = C500.2, C501.2, C502.2, C503.1, J500.3, Q500.1-3 (S), R504.2, R505.1, TP501.1, U500.6 (VSS), with no GND node. DOUT_GATE = Q500.4/TP503/U500.1. COUT_GATE = Q501.4/TP504/U500.2. B- = Q501.1-3 (S), TP502, R502.2 (V- tap), J14 even pins, J15.1, J19.1/3 and JP607.1; JP607.2 = GND. J701 A1/A12/B1/B12/S1 = GND. pos.csv: TP500-TP505 sit at (190-198, 163.5/168.5) F.Cu and none is GND; the nearest GND reference is JP607 at (217.7,145.8). The PCB silkscreen reads 'B-' at J500.3 (213.08,163.0), and J500.3 is VBAT_BENCH_N. Sheet note at (15.24,235.01): 'The PSU must FLOAT. If its negative is earthed while the FC ground is earthed (laptop, scope), VBAT_BENCH_N is shorted to GND and both protection FETs are bypassed'. No sheet text names the reference for the test points. final_list.md item 3 ATP text: 'TP503/TP504 gate drive stays high, no DOUT latch' at 2.0 A, with no reference stated. R5460 datasheet EA-165-250616: p.9 says a level shifter 'makes the L level of COUT pin to the V- pin voltage'; p.10 says 'DOUT ... H level of VDD and L level of VSS'; p.10 says excess-discharge releases only when V- is pulled down to VSS by the internal pull-down after the load is removed. review_fixes.md item 3: sense-loop copper now 7.8 mOhm.
verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism holds. VBAT_BENCH_N reaches GND only through Q500, Q501 and B- plus the inhibit (JP607/J15/J19). An earthed scope ground on TP501, or on J500.3 (silkscreened 'B-'), while J701 connects board GND to an earthed host, puts the earth loop in parallel with the protection FETs and the inhibit. The sheet describes this exact bypass for an earthed PSU negative. It does not say that TP501 sits on the same node. The TP cluster has no GND point, so clipping ground to TP501 is plausible.

The impact is overstated in three ways.
(1) A scope referenced to TP501 still reads DOUT correctly, because DOUT is measured against its own source (VSS). Item 3's ATP criterion (gate high, no latch) therefore stays readable. The real distortion is current sharing. Before any trip, the FET path (about 26 mOhm FETs plus 7.8 mOhm copper plus the inhibit jumper) shares current with an earth loop of a few hundred mOhm. That diverts roughly 10-30% of the load, which raises the effective excess-discharge trip current and biases a marginal 2 A ATP toward a false pass.
(2) After any trip, the FC stays powered through the earth loop. The flowing current holds V- above VDET3, so DOUT stays latched and an over-discharge or excess-discharge trip test would wrongly show the FC staying up. The current is capped at the 2 A PSU limit and the loop is probe shield, mains earth and USB-C GND, all of which survive 2 A. There is no damage path, so this does not meet the fix-this-rev criterion.
(3) The finding says both gates are referenced to VSS. That is only true for DOUT: per EA-165 p.9, COUT's low level is V- (B- via R502), so TP504 pairs with TP502.

This is an ATP and bench-procedure wording item with no copper change. The sheet already carries the general warning, so severity drops from minor to info.
verdicts.corrected_description: TP501 (VBAT_BENCH_N, the Q500 source and U500 VSS) and J500.3 (silkscreened 'B-' but on VBAT_BENCH_N) are the natural ground-clip points for the item-3 ATP gate measurement, because the TP500-TP505 cluster has no GND point. With J701 or the FC USB on an earthed host and an earthed scope ground on either point, the earth loop parallels Q500/Q501 and the inhibit. Before a trip it diverts roughly 10-30% of the load current, raising the effective trip current and biasing the 2 A no-latch ATP toward a pass. After a DOUT trip it keeps the FC powered and carries up to the 2 A PSU limit through the probe shield and USB GND, so deliberate trip tests read wrong. There is no hardware damage at the 2 A limit. DOUT_GATE (TP503) is referenced to VSS (TP501), but COUT_GATE (TP504) is referenced to V-/B- (TP502) per EA-165 p.9. Remedy is ATP text only, next-rev or procedure: state the test-point references, measure gate drive with a floating DMM, a differential probe or an isolated scope, or clip the scope ground to board GND (e.g. JP607.2) with the inhibit/JP607 closed, and never earth TP501 or J500.3.

verdicts.reasoning: Every number reproduces: 57 items, about 25 in the bench area, the exact pads and coordinates named, and 0.5/0.5 spoke and gap. The evidence holds. The impact does not. The two places the finding calls worth a look carry no plausible failure. U511 PGND pins 19/20 do not depend on the spoke. Each has a direct F.Cu bridge into the solid-connected EP with 9 thermal vias, plus a track to a dedicated GND via, so the BQ25886 low-impedance PGND return is met regardless of the spoke. Pin 5 is the OTG logic strap, not a PGND/GND power pin, so including it as 'U511 GND/PGND' is a small mislabel. The J510 GND pads really do have only the spoke: one 0.5 mm wide, 0.5 mm long spoke per pad location on 1 oz outer copper. That is about 0.5 mOhm each. At the 1.48 A ILIM split over two spokes, the drop is about 0.4 mV and the loss about 0.3 mW. Even with all 1.48 A in one spoke it is about 0.7 mV and 1 mW. That is two orders of magnitude below the USB-C contact resistance in series, and the GND shell PTH sits about 1.4 mm away. The single-spoke decoupling caps (C214, C220, C516 REGN) add sub-nH inductance and are not a demonstrated failure. A single spoke is not a JLC manufacturability risk; if anything it improves reflow thermal balance. The ignore setting is heritage Rev2 practice, not a FlatSat regression. The one thing that survives is a process gap: the project gate cannot see this class, and drc_triage.md reports starved_thermal 0 as 'fixed', which is vacuous. That is a valid next-rev hygiene note, not a bench failure or damage mechanism. Severity drops to info. The disposition stays next-rev with no change this rev, as the finding already says.

verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the mechanism. When COUT opens, Q501 stops only charge-direction current. The PSU sourcing into the FC is discharge-direction for the pack model: FC GND -> ISS shunt -> B- -> Q501 S->D. That is the NMOS body diode forward direction, so the FC sees V_PSU minus about 0.7 V. Above 10-12 V the R5460 leaves its operating and abs-max range anyway, and current flows either way. All rail and cap claims match the netlist and project.db. Neither the sheet nor the silk carries the item-7-style OVP procedure or a J500 voltage legend, and the first review never raised J500 OV, so this is not a re-report. The impact is somewhat understated: (a) the replica IC U500 (R5460) has a 12 V VDD abs max and a 10 V operating max, so above 12 V the replica itself is overstressed and later Mode-1 runs would test a damaged part; (b) FC-copy LT3652 IC6 BAT on VBATT_SENSE is 15 V abs max, so an 18 V setting stresses a heritage IC, not just 10 V MLCCs. The BQ25886 SYS sub-case needs JP510 fitted with a PSU on J500, which the sheet already forbids ('Never fit JP510 with a PSU on J500'). That makes it a double fault and weak support. Severity stays minor: operator error against a documented window, the same class and precedent as item 7 (minor, text-only this rev). A cheap text/procedure action this rev is consistent with item 7. A hardware OV cut-off belongs next rev.

The high-side chain is VBATT_SENSE -J8/JP602- INHIB_1 -J29/JP603- IN_RBF -J20/J30/JP606- VBUSP, with a parallel J7/JP604 - INHIB_2 - J10/JP605 path. Sheet texts: replica sheet line 13102 'B- ... reaches GND only through the ISS inhibit J15/J19' and line 13201 'Mode 2 USB charger: JP500 OPEN, JP510 fitted, bench PSU disconnected at J500. The FC runs from U511 SYS'. pyro_inhibit.kicad_sch:4165 power-up recipe 'bridge JP607 (B- return) + JP606 (RBF) + ONE inhibit path', plus its warning that FC USB J12 powers VBUSP 'regardless of every jumper'. First review final_list line 133 already notes 'Mode 2 returns through board GND, JP500 open, no pack per D11', but only as a sub-claim refutation, not as an ISS item. Phase-1 brief hard rule 6 = 'Nothing in series with a flight power path', not 'inhibit chain fidelity'.
verdicts.reasoning: The topology claim reproduces exactly. In Mode 2 the FC load current returns through board GND to U511/J510, never through B-, so opening J15/J19/JP607 does not de-power the FC. The replica is also out of the path, which is by design and implied by the Mode 2 line. The impact is overstated. (1) ISS inhibit is a battery-return break. Mode 2 has no battery (D11), and every other ground-referenced source in the heritage design bypasses it the same way: the solar path through the LT3652, and FC USB J12/D15. The pyro sheet already warns of the latter. So this is the expected behaviour of a non-battery source, not a defect. (2) The high-side inhibit chain (S1/S2/P1/P2/RBF shunts and crimps) and SW600 still act in Mode 2. Pulling JP606/RBF still opens VBUSP, so 'all jumpers open' still safes the bus. (3) The 'checks pass the wrong way' framing is wrong in direction. An 'ISS open -> bus dead' check run in Mode 2 fails visibly; it does not pass silently. No hardware can be damaged, and the bench runs at 8.4 V and 1.48 A. The real residue is a documentation gap: the pyro-sheet power-up recipe calls JP607 the 'B- return' needed for power, which holds only in Mode 1, and nothing says the ISS inhibit does not safe the bus in Mode 2. That warrants a one-line sheet and procedure note, next rev or with any open text edit. The cited 'brief hard rule 6 (inhibit chain fidelity)' is misattributed.
verdicts.corrected_description: In Mode 2 the BQ25886 charger output (CHG_SYS -> JP510 -> Dir_Chrg_In) returns through board GND (U511 PGND/EP, J510 GND), not through B-. The ISS inhibit (J15/J19/JP607) is therefore not in the FC power path, and opening it leaves the FC powered. The high-side S1/S2/P1/P2/RBF chain and SW600 still act. This is inherent to a non-battery source: solar and FC USB J12 bypass ISS the same way in heritage. The R5460 replica is out of circuit by design. Documentation gap only: the pyro-sheet power-up recipe lists JP607 as the required 'B- return', which is true only in Mode 1. Add a Mode 2 note: 'ISS inhibit and the R5460 replica are not in circuit in Mode 2; use JP606/RBF to safe the bus; run ISS-inhibit and protection tests in Mode 1 only.' No hardware change.

verdicts.reasoning: All geometry reproduces to within 0.05 mm. REGN is a real deviation from SLUSD88A 11.1 item 4. The cap is next to the IC, but it faces the pin with its GND pad. The REGN connection is 7 mm with two vias where a 180-degree rotation gives about 1.3 mm of F.Cu with no via. The first review checked REGN routing (agents.json) and did not flag it. BTST did roughly double (3.8 mm to 7.8 mm) because item 4 moved C512 to the SW run to free the SYS-pin slot for C513. That move follows TI's own priority order (item 1 SYS cap over item 4 decoupling). The 7.8 mm is close to the minimum for C512's new location (6.1 mm straight-line pin 12 to C512.2), so the remaining issue is placement, not routing. The impact is somewhat overstated. In a boost stage the BTST-supplied high-side FET is the synchronous rectifier and is soft-switched, so extra BTST loop inductance mainly shifts dead-time behaviour and does little to SW ringing. Only the REGN (low-side driver) loop affects the hard-switched edge. A few nH there means sub-volt REGN bounce, far from the 6 V abs max. The datasheet has no REGN UVLO, so the 'droop near UVLO' path is speculative. Small inaccuracies: the In1 REGN segment runs from U511's south-east corner under C516, not under the U511 body. It passes about 0.7 mm south of the straight line from the C513 GND vias (281.0/281.95,156.35) to the EP vias, so it does not cut that return path. No failure or damage is plausible on this bench board, so this stays minor / next-rev. Adding a REGN probe point to the existing item-4 SW scope check is a cheap, reasonable this-rev mitigation.
verdicts.corrected_description: BQ25886 U511 REGN bypass C516 (4.7 uF) is placed next to the IC, but it is rotated so its GND pad faces pin 11. The REGN connection is therefore 7.0 mm of 0.25 mm track with two 0.46/0.20 vias (F.Cu -> In1 -> F.Cu) where about 1.3 mm of F.Cu with no via was possible. This deviates from SLUSD88A 11.1 item 4. The routing was present at the first review and was not flagged. Item 4 moved C512 (BTST 47 nF) onto the SW run north-east of U511 to free the SYS-pin slot for C513 (TI priority 1 over priority 4). The BTST connection from south-edge pin 12 grew from 3.8 mm (In2, 2 vias) to 7.8 mm (B.Cu along x=279.4, 2 vias). Expected effect: a few nH of extra gate-drive loop inductance. It matters mostly on the REGN/low-side (hard-switched) loop. The BTST/high-side synchronous-rectifier loop is soft-switched and much less sensitive. No damage mechanism is shown. Next rev: rotate C516 180 degrees and route it on F.Cu, and try C512 at the south-east corner. This rev: add a REGN probe to the item-4 SW scope check.

verdicts.reasoning: The geometry, the series-only topology and the rule's lack of a layer condition all reproduce. The thermal consequence does not hold. At 2 A each run dissipates only about 3.9 mW/mm: (a) about 35 mW, (b) about 52 mW, (c) about 36 mW. Each run sits 0.21 mm from a GND plane, and the IPC-2221 internal curve (the 86-102 C figures) is known to be inapplicable to short traces next to planes. A conduction estimate (q'*t/(k*w) = 3.9 W/m * 0.21 mm / (0.3 W/mK * 1 mm), about 3 C to the plane, plus a few C of plane rise for ~0.12 W total) puts realistic rise at roughly 10 C or less at the 2 A PSU limit, below the reviewer's own 10-20 C IPC-2152 estimate. Copper resistance is ~31 mOhm in total (~60 mV at 2 A), consistent with item 2's 34.7 mOhm J500.1->J14.1 figure. The 20 C criterion the reviewer compares against belonged to the removed heritage path. Segments (b) and (c) are unchanged since the first review accepted them. Segment (a) meets the item-2 action (>=1.0 mm, any layer), and review_fixes.md documents why In1 was the only free layer at J14.1. The brief-L5 'on F.Cu/B.Cu' wording is an internal-brief deviation, not a manufacturer or failure issue. The one hotter spot on this path, the 0.3 mm F.Cu VBAT_BENCH_N neck, is already a known deferred residual. No failure or damage mechanism remains, and the proposed 1.5 A interim cap is unnecessary. What is left is a process note: the bench_power_width rule could be layer-aware next rev.

result.summary: Second-pass principal PCB merge of 10 kept findings into 7 items (2 merges: ids 4+13 Mode-2 ISS bypass, ids 2+10 BQ25886 gate-drive caps). The six first-review fixes check out in the packet evidence: item 1 (JP510.1 = CHG_SYS), item 2 (new 1.1 mm In1 stub to J14.1, J16.8 path gone, no 1.5 A cap needed), item 3 (sense loop 7.8 mOhm), item 4 (C513 at SYS, 9 EP PTH vias, GND vias at caps), item 6 (bench_power_width rule present, one process gap: not layer-aware), item 7 (18 V text and OVP procedure on the solar sheet). No fix introduced a bench-failure or damage defect. Two small regressions from the rework are recorded as next-rev with this-rev bench probes: item 4 lengthened the BTST trace (loop area no worse) and via-in-pad batch b1 left C216.2/Y200.4 on a via-less F.Cu island. The one fix-this-rev item is new and text-only: J500 has no over-voltage element and, unlike J400/J401 after item 7, no PSU-OVP trip procedure or voltage legend; the R5460 trip does not block PSU current through the Q501 body diode, so a 12-18 V supply (the VSOLAR PSU sits 16 mm away on the same terminal row) would put 1.2-1.8x rating on FC-copy 10 V caps C42/C1/C3, exceed U500 R5460 VDD abs max and, above 15 V, LT3652 IC6 BAT. Same class and precedent as first-review item 7 (minor / fix-this-rev / trivial). J510 USB-C recess (2.4 mm, vs 1.2 mm flown J12) could not be settled: the HRO drawing is not retrievable and the KiCad footprint carries no edge line; it goes to a pre-order test fit. Dropped: VREG_AVDD C215/C218 swap (verifier: negligible, documented, inside item 5), starved_thermal (heritage Rev2 setting, no electrical consequence), and the refuted FT-GPIO pull-up finding. Zero copper changes recommended this rev.

items.rationale: Packet id 12, verifier confirmed. Above VDET1 (8.5 V) the R5460 opens COUT, but PSU current into the FC is discharge-direction for the pack model (FC GND -> ISS shunt -> B- -> Q501 source-to-drain = body-diode forward), so Dir_Chrg_In sees V_PSU - 0.7 V. At 12-18 V that is 1.2-1.8x rating on C42/C1/C3 (C19702, 10 uF 10 V X5R), above the U500 R5460 VDD abs max of 12 V (EA-165, operating max 10 V) and above 15 V the FC-copy LT3652 IC6 BAT abs max. A shorted FC-copy MLCC dumps PSU current (2 A limit) into frozen FC copper, the one outcome this board must avoid. The hazard is operator error against a documented window, but the VSOLAR bench supply on the adjacent terminals runs at 12-18 V and item 7 was written for exactly this reuse case; J500 got neither the OVP procedure nor the legend. First-review item 7 set the precedent: text-only hazard mitigation = fix-this-rev / trivial. The BQ25886 SYS 12 V sub-case needs JP510 fitted with a PSU on J500, which the sheet already forbids, so it adds no weight. No copper change. First review items 7/9/10 never raised J500 over-voltage, so this is not a re-report.

items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch lines 13102 (B- note), 13201 (Mode 2 line); pyro_inhibit.kicad_sch line ~4165 POWER-UP RECIPE ('bridge JP607 (B- return) + JP606 (RBF) + ONE inhibit path'). Netlist: U511 pins 4/19/20/25 = GND, J510 GND; JP510.1 = CHG_SYS, JP510.2 = Dir_Chrg_In; B- = Q501.1-3, J14.2/4/6/8, J15.1, J19.1/3, JP607.1 (no GND member); JP607.2/J15.2/J19.2/4 = GND.
items.rationale: Merges packet ids 4 and 13, both verifier-confirmed and downgraded to info. Topology reproduces: in Mode 2 the FC load returns to U511/J510 on board GND, never through B-, so opening J15/J19/JP607 leaves the FC powered. This was not introduced by fix item 1 (the old CHG_BAT feed was equally GND-referenced) and it is inherent to any non-battery source: heritage solar via the LT3652 and FC USB J12/D15 bypass the ISS inhibit the same way, and the pyro sheet already warns of the latter. The high-side S1/S2/P1/P2/RBF chain and SW600 still act, so 'all jumpers open' still safes the bus via JP606. An 'ISS open -> bus dead' check run in Mode 2 fails visibly rather than passing silently. No hardware risk at 8.4 V / 1.48 A. Residue is a documentation gap: the pyro recipe presents JP607 as required for power, true only in Mode 1, and nothing states the Mode 2 exemption. Text only; bundle with the rank-1 sheet edit if the sheet is reopened.

items.location: FlatSat_V1.kicad_pcb J510 Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12 at (262.0,166.06) rot 0; F.Fab front y=169.71; Edge.Cuts y=172.12 (straight, no notch). HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing (LCSC C165948), RECOMMEND P.C.B LAYOUT: PCB EDGE 5.79 from the 0.60 peg-hole centre = footprint rel +3.19 (front face rel +3.65)
items.rationale: Resolved the verifier's 'uncertain' by reading the HRO drawing: PCB EDGE is 5.79 mm from the peg-hole centre (peg rel -2.60, front slot +1.05, 4.18 slot pitch and 2.60 front-leg-to-face all match the KiCad footprint), so HRO wants the connector front 0.46 mm proud of the edge. That makes the 6.65 mm plug shell bottom at 6.19 mm = receptacle depth. J510 instead has 2.41 mm of FR4 in front of the face; the plug axis is 1.63 mm above the board (3.26 mm shell), so any overmold taller than ~3.3 mm hits the lip after 6.65-2.41 = 4.24 mm of insertion, ~2 mm short of full. Flown J12 (1.19 mm recess, ~0.7 mm short) and J701 (0.64 mm) mate; J510 is 1.2 mm deeper than the worst case known to work. Partial seat means no latch and intermittent VBUS at 1.48 A, i.e. Mode 2 (the SYS feed that item 1 just moved the FC onto) is unusable with ordinary cables. Workarounds exist (TP510 breakout, slim-overmold cable), so this is a functional loss, not damage. The strip x 250-274, y 168.5-172.5 contains no tracks, vias or footprints on any layer, so the move only drags J510's own pad escapes and refills GND; J510 is outside FC_COPY so heritage.py is unaffected.

items.rationale: Both principals rank 1, minor, fix-this-rev, trivial; verifier confirmed. C42/C1/C3 are C19702 10 uF 10 V X5R; U500 R5460 VDD abs max 12 V (operating 10 V, EA-165); IC6 LT3652 BAT abs max 15 V. The bench already runs 12-18 V on J400/J401 16 mm away in the same Phoenix family, and first-review item 7 gave those terminals an OVP pre-session check and an '18V MAX' legend; J500 got neither. A shorted FC-copy MLCC would dump PSU current (2 A limit) into frozen FC copper, the outcome this board must avoid. Operator error against a documented window, same class and precedent as item 7: text-only mitigation this rev. The BQ25886 SYS 12 V sub-case needs JP510 fitted with a PSU on J500, already forbidden at line 13179, so it adds nothing. Not a re-report: items 7/9/10 never raised J500 over-voltage.
